notes: Read session_orchestrator together with continuation_policy and SessionArtifactStore. Session-visible phase is surfaced through task_progress; kernel PhaseManager remains the phase SSOT and is bridged through canonical turn history and checkpoint state, not role-profile schema. Role object instantiation uses instantiate_role_runtime_object(InstantiateRoleRuntimeObjectCommandV1) to query roles.profile through GetRoleProfileQueryV1 and bind only profile/tool/prompt/data refs plus profile_fingerprint; RoleProfileBinding rejects any owner or profile/policy ref namespace outside roles.profile; RoleRuntimeObject also carries a refs-only RoleTurnContext, and built-in specs derive typed input, context snapshot, and task refs from RoleIdentity when an explicit turn context is not supplied; RoleRuntimeObject requires its current RoleCapabilityFingerprint to point to a mounted capability port and to match that port's effect and endpoint/tool, so stale or fabricated fingerprints cannot enter a stateful role instance; RoleCapabilityFingerprint rejects caller-supplied fingerprint overrides that are not the 64-character sha256 value derived from role, capability, effect, tool, policy fingerprint, and profile fingerprint fields; InstantiateRoleRuntimeObjectCommandV1 and specs may receive an explicit RoleTaskMarketBinding at instantiation time to bind the object to current Task Market work item or lease refs while roles.runtime still stores refs only and does not own profile, turn, or Task Market state; if that binding names an active runtime.task_market:task:* work item, RoleRuntimeObject requires the ref to be present in the current RoleTurnContext.task_refs, while queue/stage refs such as runtime.task_market:pending_design remain refs-only routing bindings. RoleRuntimeObjectSpec and RoleRuntimeObject reject any mounted capability port whose allowed_roles does not include the instantiated role, so a role object cannot carry latent RPC/API ports that would be denied only at invocation time. RoleTurnEnvelope rejects identity/profile role mismatches, capability invocations whose role_id does not match the envelope identity, invocation payload refs outside the current typed input or task refs, and active runtime.task_market:task:* work refs outside the current turn_context.task_refs so inconsistent typed envelopes cannot enter ledger/commit boundaries. RoleTurnContext rejects typed input refs outside roles.runtime or runtime.task_market, context snapshot refs outside context.engine or roles.session, handoff refs outside factory.cognitive_runtime, and task refs outside the latest runtime.task_market:task:<task_id> shape. Role asset mount tables, capability descriptors, and capability ports reject roles.runtime, role adapter/kernel/profile/session cells, and kernelone.roles paths as owners; asset mount refs also reject role-runtime and KernelOne role-template namespaces, and their ref namespace must match owner_cell. The only built-in graph-derived exception is Architect ConstraintTopology, where context.catalog may expose a docs.graph:* ref when graph_source_ref anchors the asset to docs/graph/**. Business assets and capabilities must be owned by their real business or platform state Cell and mounted only by public contract/ref. Capability endpoint_ref values must point to the same owner Cell public contract, either through owner_cell:* logical refs or polaris.cells.<owner_cell>.public.* module refs. RoleRuntimeObjectSpec validates capability metadata keys such as requires_asset_mounts, asset_mount, input_asset_mount, output_asset_mount, and evidence_asset_mount against the RoleAssetMountTable so a capability port cannot claim an unmounted role asset dependency. The KernelOne release gate scans all roles.runtime owned Python paths from cell.yaml (public/**, internal/**, role_chat.py, and role_session.py) and rejects cross-Cell polaris.cells.*.internal imports before release; it also scans polaris/kernelone/roles/** and rejects business-role filenames or Python definitions for PM, Chief Engineer, Architect, QA, and Director so KernelOne stays limited to shared types and low-level role templates. Role task-market lifecycle uses execute_role_task_market_lifecycle(ExecuteRoleTaskMarketLifecycleCommandV1) to translate role-bound publish/claim/lease/ack/fail/requeue operations into runtime.task_market public contracts; RoleTaskMarketBinding rejects active work item and lease token refs outside runtime.task_market and old active work refs such as runtime.task_market:task-1; lease/ack/fail/requeue additionally require payload.task_id to resolve to a runtime.task_market task ref listed in the runtime object current RoleTurnContext.task_refs before Task Market public service calls; every lifecycle operation also requires a mounted runtime.task_market capability port whose public contract matches the lifecycle command, whose allowed_roles contains the current role, and whose capability/effect/tool match the runtime object's current RoleCapabilityFingerprint; lease/ack/fail additionally require payload.lease_token to match the runtime object's active RoleTaskMarketBinding.lease_token_ref. Role capability invocation is latest-only: RoleCapabilityInvocation rejects payload refs outside roles.runtime or runtime.task_market and requires a 64-character hex capability fingerprint value; RoleCapabilityDecision evidence refs must point to audit.evidence; RoleCapabilityInvocationResultV1 rejects role runtime/kernel/profile/session owner cells, requires target result refs to point to the declared owner Cell, and only permits non-result payload refs from runtime typed input or task-market refs; failed capability invocation results must always report allowed=false, while capability discoverability is represented only by metadata.capability_available; after fingerprint unlock and before any target Cell public call, execute_role_capability_invocation requires invocation.payload_ref to match the runtime object current RoleTurnContext typed input ref or task refs and requires the runtime object current RoleCapabilityFingerprint capability id, effect, and endpoint/tool to match the mounted capability port; the KernelOne release gate enforces failed-result semantics with an AST check against public runtime code, rejecting static RoleCapabilityInvocationResultV1(ok=False, allowed=True) constructors before release; mounted ports reject empty allowed_roles and validate role allow-lists, capability fingerprints, command contracts, and current-turn payload refs, then delegate to target Cell public APIs such as runtime.task_market PublishTaskWorkItemCommandV1 / QueryTaskMarketStatusV1, runtime.projection RuntimeProjectionQueryV1, chief_engineer.blueprint GenerateTaskBlueprintCommandV1, code_intelligence.engine VerifyAstDependencyQueryV1, factory.verification_guard VerifyCompletionCommandV1, qa.audit_verdict RunQaAuditCommandV1 / ParseTracebackFramesCommandV1 / RunVisualQaAuditCommandV1, finops.budget_guard ReserveBudgetCommandV1, and policy.workspace_guard WorkspaceWriteGuardBatchQueryV1. Chief Engineer blueprint delegation carries mounted BlueprintDatabase, ArchConstraintMemo, and DiffMapArchive refs in typed command context/result metadata so roles.runtime never owns those assets. PM critical-path evaluation derives task DAG dependency edges, failed stages, projection refs, and mounted asset refs from runtime.task_market QueryTaskMarketStatusV1 results; it does not scan scattered files or own task state. QA pytest verification requires both role_id=qa and the QA capability fingerprint before building VerifyCompletionCommandV1, so misconfigured non-QA ports are rejected without calling factory.verification_guard. QA visual audit first queries llm.control_plane CheckLlmModelCapabilityQueryV1 and requires an explicit image_input capability ref before building RunVisualQaAuditCommandV1; the preflight query is bound to the current runtime role_id, payload llm_role is audit metadata only, the required model capability comes from the mounted descriptor, payload downgrade attempts return allowed=false before model preflight, and text-only models do not invoke QA. Architect boundary validation uses policy.permission EvaluatePermissionCommandV1, policy.workspace_guard WorkspaceWriteGuardBatchQueryV1, and architect.design GenerateArchitectureDesignCommandV1 through public services; empty changed_paths are denied before permission/guard/design calls, and sandbox denials return allowed=false. Role state commit uses commit_role_state(RoleStateCommitRequest) to bind an existing roles.kernel CommitReceipt ref to factory.cognitive_runtime ValidateChangeSetCommandV1, RecordRuntimeReceiptCommandV1, and ExportHandoffPackCommandV1; RoleStateCommitRequest rejects changed asset refs outside the current RoleTurnContext.task_refs, rejects evidence refs outside audit.evidence, requires changed files to be relative paths under explicit allowed_scope_paths before Cognitive Runtime validation or receipt recording can run, and rejects empty commits that omit changed asset refs, changed files, and audit evidence refs; successful RoleStateCommitReceipt values must include both the kernel CommitReceipt ref and at least one Cognitive Runtime receipt ref; ledger/commit/turn outcome refs must point to roles.kernel, and runtime receipt, handoff, and change-set refs must point to factory.cognitive_runtime. roles.runtime stores refs only and does not create a second ledger, change-set validator, handoff system, or receipt store. Director task execution delegates to director.execution ExecuteDirectorTaskCommandV1 via director.execution.public.service.execute_director_task while mounting only ExecutionTask, DirectorExecutionState, and DirectorEvidenceTrail refs; roles.runtime keeps result/evidence refs only. Phase 5 chain assembly uses AssembleRoleRuntimeChainCommandV1 to produce a refs-only RoleRuntimeChainEnvelope across PM, Chief Engineer, Director, QA, audit evidence, Turn Ledger, runtime receipts, handoff refs, Task Market refs, Runtime Projection refs, and per-step capability fingerprint refs without creating a second Task Market, ledger, handoff pack, receipt store, or projection. RoleRuntimeChainEnvelope rejects aggregate refs that omit step task/work-item, evidence, capability fingerprint, handoff, or runtime receipt refs; RoleRuntimeChainStepRef rejects role runtime/kernel/profile/session and KernelOne role-template owner cells, requires result_ref to point to its owner_cell, and enforces source-of-truth namespaces for task market, evidence, fingerprint, handoff, receipt, projection, and ledger refs.
role_turn_envelope_invariants: RoleTurnEnvelope rejects duplicate capability invocation ids so Turn Ledger audit entries cannot collapse multiple capability calls under one invocation identity.
role_asset_mount_invariants: DiffMapArchive asset mounts that declare requires_blueprint_ref must include blueprint_id, path, and ref metadata so Chief Engineer diff/spec assets remain anchored to a chief_engineer.blueprint asset instead of natural-language state.
OpenLoopRegistry asset mounts must include evidence_owner_cell=audit.evidence and an audit.evidence evidence_ref so PM open-loop state remains anchored to Task Market and Audit Evidence owner Cells.

TruthLog asset mounts must include runtime_receipt_owner_cell=factory.cognitive_runtime and a factory.cognitive_runtime runtime_receipt_ref so QA truth logs stay anchored to Audit Evidence and Cognitive Runtime receipts.
role_task_market_lifecycle_invariants: RoleTaskMarketLifecycleResultV1 requires every successful task-market lifecycle result to include a runtime.task_market result_ref so publish/claim/lease/ack/fail/requeue/dead-letter successes are anchored to the Task Market owner Cell.
Dead-letter role lifecycle operations delegate to runtime.task_market MoveTaskToDeadLetterCommandV1 through a mounted capability fingerprint and never create a second DLQ state owner.

execute_role_task_market_lifecycle returns task_market_lifecycle_missing_result_ref for malformed upstream ok=true task-market responses without a task id/ref instead of exposing an unauditable success.
RoleTaskMarketLifecycleResultV1 requires successful claim/lease lifecycle results to include a runtime.task_market lease_token_ref so active leases remain auditable.
execute_role_task_market_lifecycle returns task_market_lifecycle_missing_lease_ref for malformed upstream ok=true claim/lease responses without a lease token/ref.
role_capability_invocation_result_invari: RoleCapabilityInvocationResultV1 requires every successful capability result to include a target owner_cell and result_ref so successful RPC/API calls are anchored to the owning public Cell.
RoleCapabilityInvocationResultV1 rejects evidence refs outside audit.evidence and rejects duplicate evidence refs so capability results cannot carry foreign or collapsed audit anchors.
Role capability results normalize owner-service runtime/evidence/** paths into audit.evidence:path:* refs before exposing evidence_refs, including Director execution and QA audit verdict results.

QA visual audit capability successes must include an audit.evidence evidence ref; roles.runtime maps owner-service runtime/evidence/** receipt paths to audit.evidence:path:* refs and rejects unaudited visual audit success results.
role_state_commit_invariants: RoleStateCommitRequest rejects empty commits that omit changed asset refs, changed files, and audit evidence refs.
RoleStateCommitReceipt rejects duplicate factory.cognitive_runtime runtime receipt and handoff refs instead of silently collapsing audit anchors.
role_handoff_rehydration_invariants: rehydrate_role_handoff delegates to factory.cognitive_runtime RehydrateHandoffPackCommandV1 and returns only factory.cognitive_runtime rehydration/receipt refs plus roles.session artifact/episode refs.
RoleHandoffRehydrationResultV1 rejects successful handoff rehydration results without a factory.cognitive_runtime rehydration ref.
rehydrate_role_handoff normalizes raw Cognitive Runtime receipt/artifact/episode ids into factory.cognitive_runtime or roles.session owner refs before returning the runtime public result.
latest_runtime_path_invariants: KernelOne release gate rejects production Python files under polaris/application, polaris/cells, and polaris/delivery that directly import or construct RoleExecutionKernel outside the roles.kernel owner Cell and roles.runtime.public.service composition boundary.

KernelOne release gate rejects production Python files under polaris/application, polaris/cells, and polaris/delivery that import or call llm.dialogue role compatibility functions generate_role_response or generate_role_response_streaming outside the llm.dialogue owner Cell.
Production role execution must enter RoleRuntimeService so runtime-object/session/ledger preflight remains the only route to RoleExecutionKernel.
phase5_chain_invariants: RoleRuntimeChainStepRef must include task_ref or work_item_ref so every chain step is anchored to runtime.task_market.
RoleRuntimeChainStepRef.task_ref must use runtime.task_market:task:<task_id>; unqualified runtime.task_market:task-1 refs are rejected before chain assembly.
assemble_role_runtime_chain rejects required role steps that violate declared required_roles order, preserving the PM -> Chief Engineer -> Director -> QA Phase 5 chain.
assemble_role_runtime_chain rejects callers that include all default PM -> Chief Engineer -> Director -> QA steps but downgrade required_roles to a subset.
A complete default PM -> Chief Engineer -> Director -> QA Phase 5 chain must include at least one runtime.projection ref before assembly succeeds.
A complete default PM -> Chief Engineer -> Director -> QA Phase 5 chain must include at least one audit.evidence ref before assembly succeeds.
A complete default PM -> Chief Engineer -> Director -> QA Phase 5 chain must include audit.evidence refs on the Director and QA steps before assembly succeeds.

A complete default PM -> Chief Engineer -> Director -> QA Phase 5 chain must include factory.cognitive_runtime handoff refs on the Chief Engineer -> Director and Director -> QA role transitions before assembly succeeds.

A complete default PM -> Chief Engineer -> Director -> QA Phase 5 chain must include factory.cognitive_runtime runtime receipt refs for Chief Engineer, Director, and QA execution steps before assembly succeeds.

assemble_role_runtime_chain returns typed RoleRuntimeChainAssemblyResultV1 failures for invalid aggregate Turn Ledger, Runtime Projection, or Audit Evidence owner refs instead of leaking RoleRuntimeChainEnvelope constructor exceptions.
RoleRuntimeChainEnvelope remains refs-only and must aggregate each step task/work-item, evidence, capability fingerprint, handoff, and runtime receipt ref under the real owner namespaces.
